title: Best Indian Coming-of-Age Films
description: The Indian films that captured what it felt like to grow up here.
intro: Coming of age in India carries its own rhythms — these films know them.

entries.why_it_ranks: Friendship, education pressure, parental expectations and the courage to define success for yourself make it perhaps India's most influential mainstream coming-of-age film.
A landmark portrayal of urban Indian friendship in which three young men discover that adulthood inevitably changes relationships, priorities and themselves.
George's journey through school, college and adulthood uses love and heartbreak to show how experiences gradually shape a person.
A carefree teenager learns responsibility, discipline and self-respect in one of Hindi cinema's most enduring youth films.
Three cousins arrive in Bengaluru with different dreams and gradually confront careers, marriage, disappointment, relationships and adulthood.
A powerful story of a teenager confronting an authoritarian father while fighting for the right to choose his own identity and future.
Four dysfunctional brothers gradually learning responsibility, affection and what makes a family gives the film a beautiful collective maturation arc.
A privileged, directionless young man gradually discovers work, independence, love and a sense of purpose.
Young people constrained by grief, caste and social judgment struggle to move beyond the identities society has imposed upon them.
An exceptionally natural portrayal of teenage insecurity, crushes, jealousy, friendship and school life.
Love, heartbreak, addiction, family and self-discovery shape Surya's long journey from youth toward emotional maturity.
Two children's simple desire to taste pizza becomes their introduction to money, class, consumerism and the adult world.
Boarding school, friendship, bullying, attraction and independence are captured with unusual warmth and authenticity.
Engineering-college friendships, first romances and conflicts capture the excitement and eventual bittersweet ending of student life.
College, romance, heartbreak, mistakes, career and eventually family life chart a young man's gradual transition into adulthood.
Karna begins as an irresponsible engineering student before friendship, love, tragedy and time fundamentally change him.
An adult revisiting the people who shaped his life becomes a reflective journey through adolescence, love, heartbreak and maturity.
Murad's discovery of his artistic voice becomes a larger journey toward confidence, independence and escaping the future others expect him to accept.
A group of immature friends encounter romance, rebellion, music and consequences that gradually force them to take responsibility.
Friendship slowly developing into romantic awareness gives the film an enduring youthful warmth.
A deaf and mute village boy's dream of becoming a cricketer becomes an inspiring journey of confidence, independence and perseverance.
June grows from an awkward schoolgirl through college, relationships and heartbreak into an adult increasingly comfortable with herself.
A teenager's innocent attraction collides painfully with caste and social hierarchy, turning adolescence into an awakening to the world's inequality.
A young boy adjusting to a new town and school experiences loneliness, friendship and change in one of India's gentlest childhood coming-of-age films.
Teenage romance, class difference and first heartbreak give this popular film genuine coming-of-age emotion.
